strings.main.folders.tip: Photos from all these folders (and their subfolders) make up the library: they are used as tiles. Delete removes the selected folders from the list.
strings.main.remove_folder.tip: Remove the selected folders from the list (the files are not touched)
strings.main.suggest: Suggest a target picture from my photos…
strings.main.suggest.tip: Ranks the photos of your library by how good a mosaic each would make.
strings.main.tile_size.tip: Size of one tile in the saved mosaic. Bigger tiles = photos easier to recognize up close, bigger file.
strings.main.output.unknown: The output size depends on the target picture.
strings.main.grid.tip:
Each cell and each tile is compared as an N × N grid of average colors.
1 — only the average color; 3 — also where it is lighter or darker (recommended); 6 — finer, slower.
strings.main.repeat.tip:
How far apart the same photo may appear.
More — fewer visible repeats, but cells more often get a photo of a less exact color.
0 — the best photo for each cell, repeats can stand side by side.
strings.main.variety.tip:
How strongly to spread the work over different photos.
More — more of your photos appear in the mosaic, colors a little less exact.
Less — the best-matching photos are used again and again.
strings.main.correction.tip:
Shifts each tile's average color toward the color of its cell; the photo's details stay.
0 % — tiles keep their own colors; 50 % — halfway to the cell's color; 100 % — every tile has exactly its cell's average color.
strings.main.overlay.tip:
Lays the target picture over the tiles.
0 % — tiles only; 50 % — half picture, half tiles; 100 % — only the picture is visible.
strings.main.edges.tip:
Transition from one tile to the next, as a share of the tile size.
0 % — sharp edges; 10 % — neighbouring tiles fade into each other over a band a tenth of a tile wide; 25 % — over a quarter of a tile (the softest).
strings.main.look.hint: Applied to a finished mosaic instantly.
strings.main.save.tip: Saves the whole mosaic at full size (Ctrl+S). The file name gets the date and time, so several mosaics of one picture never overwrite each other.
strings.main.save_fragment.tip: Choose a part of the mosaic with a frame and save it (Ctrl+Shift+S). The fragment's photos are read again from disk at a bigger tile size (up to 4× the mosaic's tile size), so they stay sharp. A moment after the frame stops moving, the part inside it is shown that way.
strings.main.fragment.hint: Drag the frame to move it, drag a corner or turn the wheel to resize it; Ctrl+wheel zooms. Enter or double-click — save, Esc — cancel.

strings.suggest.intro: The photos of your library ranked by how good a mosaic each would make; scroll down for more. The weights on the right re-rank them instantly; “i” explains each one.
strings.suggest.ratios: The further right a slider is, the more it decides which photos come first; at 0 it does not matter.
strings.suggest.score.help:
For every photo the program builds a small trial mosaic from your library and compares the photos with each other on three points: color match, color variety and contrast. The sliders decide what matters most to you. The score next to a photo shows how well it fits these wishes compared with your other photos.
The detail range below them does not change the score: it leaves out the simplest and the most detailed photos.
Hover over a photo to see how it does on each point.
strings.suggest.status.pick: . Double-click a photo to use it.
strings.suggest.status.all_zero: . All sliders are at 0: color match, color variety and contrast count equally
strings.suggest.status.in_range: {0:N0} of {1:N0} analyzed photos in the detail range, best first
strings.weight.color_match.help:
Right — pictures in colors your library has plenty of: the mosaic comes out close to the original.
Left — colors hardly matter: pictures in colors you have few photos of can come up (color correction can make up for it).
strings.weight.color_variety.help:
Right — colorful pictures: sea and sunset, a city, flowers. They use many different photos.
Left — single-tone pictures are fine too: forest, snow, black-and-white.
strings.weight.contrast.help:
Right — pictures with clear light and dark shapes that are recognizable from a distance: silhouettes, sky above land, a lit subject on a dark background.
Left — soft, misty and evenly lit pictures are fine too.
strings.weight.detail.help:
Leaves out the photos with the least and the most detail. Photos are sorted from the simplest to the most detailed: the left handle cuts off that percent of the simplest ones, the right handle keeps photos up to that percent. For example, 10–90 % leaves out a tenth of each.
Simple pictures with large shapes (sky, water, big objects) read best in a mosaic; in detailed ones (streets, crowds, foliage) tiles follow the contours, but the smallest things get lost.
The range does not change the score.
